predecessors.name: Denmark-Norway
predecessors.text: Denmark with Schleswig and Holstein, Iceland and the Faroe Islands: what the Danish crown kept at the Treaty of Kiel of 14 January 1814

successors.name: Nazi Germany
successors.text: Denmark proper, occupied by German forces from 9 April 1940 (197 of the 202 cells of the 1936 shape lie in Cliopatria's Nazi Germany shape of 1940-1944)

successors.name: Kingdom of Denmark
successors.text: the Danish state after the German surrender; 'On 5 May 1945, Denmark was officially free of German control'

ledger.x: 14 January 1814: the Treaty of Kiel leaves the Danish crown without Norway.
1815: Denmark receives Lauenburg at the Congress of Vienna.
March 1848: Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg rebel.
30 October 1864: Jutland stays Danish; the page says 'Denmark kept the island of Ærø and some other areas' and does not date the end of the occupation of Jutland, so the treaty date is used.
30 October 1864: 'Denmark ceded Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg to Prussia and Austria.'
30 October 1864: the Austrian share of the same cession.
1 December 1918: Iceland becomes a sovereign kingdom.
10 July 1920: North Schleswig returns to Denmark.
9 April 1940: Germany invades and occupies Denmark.

wars.name: First Schleswig War
wars.outcome: Danish victory, 'Status quo ante bellum': Prussia made peace with Denmark at Berlin on 2 July 1850, the Danes won at Idstedt on 24-25 July 1850, the rebel army was disbanded on 1 April 1851 and the London Protocol of 8 May 1852 closed the settlement.

wars.name: Second Schleswig War
wars.outcome: Austro-Prussian victory: the Treaty of Vienna of 30 October 1864 gave Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg to Prussia and Austria; the Danish monarchy lost 40% of its land area; Denmark kept Ærø and some other areas.

wars.name: German invasion of Denmark (9 April 1940)
wars.outcome: German occupation of Denmark from 9 April 1940 to 5 May 1945, without annexation; British forces occupied the Faroe Islands from 12 April 1940.

certainty.note: Treaty lines: the Eider frontier of Schleswig and Holstein to 1864, the treaty line of 1864 and the 1920 plebiscite line; the 1848-1850 front in Schleswig between the rebels and the Danes is not a line.
